suggest:2.cnHint: 师兄在古卷中发现，某些词语____着修炼火息诀的温和方式。
suggest:2.hook: At the scroll's torn edge, a seventh line had been scraped away by someone.
suggest:2.line: 'These marks *suggest* the old master feared this formula.'

improve:2.en: Master Qingwu set a cracked spirit-stone on the table before me. 'Speak the Clarity Word over it each dawn,' she said. 'Watch how the light inside it changes.' Seven mornings later the stone glowed without a crack. My breath had begun to *improve* its form, grain by grain.
improve:2.cnHint: 弟子每日诵念净心之词，石中灵光竟日渐____。
improve:2.hook: On the eighth morning the stone was gone, replaced by a single white feather.
improve:2.line: 'Steady practice will *improve* the stone faster than force ever could.'

affect:2.en: Xiaoxing found a pressed leaf between two heavy texts — pale gold, shaped like an open hand. 'Storm-Touched Ginkgo,' she whispered. 'Even dried, it can *affect* the mind and sharpen inner sight.' We placed it back with care. The room felt colder the moment we let it go.
affect:2.cnHint: 师妹发现一片干叶，说它即便枯萎仍能____人的内心感知。
affect:2.hook: Behind the shelf where the leaf had rested, the wall bore a faint, handless script.
affect:2.line: 'A single leaf can *affect* the clearest mind if held too long.'

support:2.en: The Archive Hall rested on three stone pillars carved with words I could not yet read. Shen Wujiu said each pillar was a vow made by a founding master — a promise that would *support* the hall as long as the words held true. One pillar bore a thin crack along its lowest character.
support:2.cnHint: 藏经阁的三根石柱以誓言铭文____整座建筑的重量与灵气。
support:2.hook: Dust fell from the cracked pillar as I stepped closer to read.
support:2.line: 'A sect without honest words has no real *support* beneath it.'

hand:2.en: Among the loose pages of a water-stained manual I found a small map drawn in faded ink. A careful *hand* had marked seven peaks, six of which I knew. The seventh floated higher than any mountain on our charts, circled twice, with the word 'listen' written below it.
hand:2.cnHint: 一张泛黄地图上，某位前辈____笔标注了一座图册上从未出现的山峰。
hand:2.hook: The ink on the seventh peak was still slightly wet.
hand:2.line: 'A steady *hand* drew this — someone who had actually stood there.'

finding:2.en: Xiaoxing spent three days sorting the lower shelves. Her *finding* was quiet but heavy: a sealed box of scrolls stamped with the Cloud Sea Sect's oldest mark, recorded as burned in a fire forty years ago. She set the box on the reading table and looked at me without a word.
finding:2.cnHint: 师妹整理书架后有了一个重要____：那批据称已焚毁的古卷完好无损地藏在箱中。
finding:2.hook: The seal on the box had been fastened from the inside.
finding:2.line: 'My *finding* is this: someone lied about the fire.'

ago:2.en: The manuscript log listed a scroll borrowed two hundred years *ago* and never returned. The borrower's name was worn to shadow. Shen Wujiu pressed his thumb to the blank space and pulled it back quickly — the paper had stung him, the way a living thing stings when it wants to be left alone.
ago:2.cnHint: 借阅记录显示，一卷古籍在两百年____被借走，自此再未归还。
ago:2.hook: The name beneath Shen Wujiu's thumb print was now, somehow, legible.
ago:2.line: 'A debt made two hundred years *ago* is still a debt.'

essay:2.en: Master Qingwu left an assignment on my desk before first light: one short *essay* on why silence could be a word. No length was given. I wrote three lines, crossed them out, and wrote two more. When I looked up the window was dark again and a moth had settled on the page without moving.
essay:2.cnHint: 师尊布置了一篇____，要求弟子阐明为何'沉默'本身也是一个词。
essay:2.hook: The moth's wings, when I looked closely, were printed with characters I had just written.
essay:2.line: 'Your *essay* should answer only what silence cannot say itself.'

conversation:2.en: In the Hall of Bound Scrolls, I found a cracked jade tablet no larger than my palm. Pressed close, I heard two voices caught inside the stone — an old *conversation* between Master Qingwu and a disciple long gone, trading the lost word for windwalking. One voice wept. One fell silent. Then the tablet went cold.
conversation:2.cnHint: 我在藏经阁发现一块玉简，里面封存着师尊与某位故人的____，内容关乎一个失传的御风字诀。
conversation:2.hook: The second voice had spoken my name.
conversation:2.line: 'This *conversation* holds the last breath of a word the sect believed destroyed.'

self:2.en: Tucked between two dusty scrolls, I discovered a small bronze mirror etched with a single character I could not read. When I leaned close, the reflection showed not my face but a figure made of light — a truer *self*, Shen Wujiu whispered, that forms only when a disciple stops pretending. I set the mirror down quickly.
self:2.cnHint: 一面铜镜映出的不是我的面容，而是代表真实____的光影，师兄低声说那才是修行者本来的样子。
self:2.hook: Outside, the clouds beneath the mountain turned the color of old ink.
self:2.line: 'A disciple who cannot face their own *self* cannot master a single word.'

age:2.en: The sealed chest in the lower archive bore a lock shaped like a open mouth. Inside lay one scroll, its paper the yellow of deep *age*, so brittle that breathing on it raised a faint golden dust. Xiaoxing read the date aloud and stepped back — the scroll was older than the sect itself, older than the mountain's first rising.
age:2.cnHint: 档案室里一卷因____而泛黄的古籍，其年代竟早于云海宗建派之前，小星读出日期后悄悄退开。
age:2.hook: The golden dust slowly formed the shape of a door.
age:2.line: 'No word survives this *age* unless someone kept feeding it breath.'

future:2.en: Master Qingwu left a single folded note on my reading stone. It contained no greeting, only three words written in the script of the Cloud Sea Sect: the *future* is a herb that grows only in soil you prepare today. Below the words, a small pressed leaf crumbled to ash the moment I touched it.
future:2.cnHint: 师尊在我的读书台上留下一张字条，以宗门字体写下关于____的一句箴言，纸上那片枯叶触手成灰。
future:2.hook: The ash arranged itself into the shape of an unfamiliar character.
future:2.line: 'I write about the *future* so you understand why the present word costs so much.'

effect:2.en: I copied the healing character three times onto separate paper, each copy in a different ink. The first had no power at all. The second warmed my fingers. The third made the cut on my wrist close in a breath. Shen Wujiu nodded: the *effect* of a word grows with the sincerity behind the stroke, not with repetition alone.
effect:2.cnHint: 同一个治愈字诀抄写三遍，师兄解释说字诀的____取决于书写时的诚意，而非单纯重复。
effect:2.hook: On the fourth sheet, the ink moved by itself.
effect:2.line: 'The *effect* fades the moment your mind wanders from the meaning.'

local:2.en: Deep in the archive, I found a collection of words used only on this one floating mountain — *local* characters, Shen Wujiu explained, shaped by the particular wind and mineral cloud that rose here and nowhere else. They could not be carried down to the ground world. They worked only here, under this sky, with this air in your lungs.
local:2.cnHint: 藏经阁深处保存着一批只属于本山的____字诀，师兄说它们离开此地便会失效。
local:2.hook: One of those characters had been freshly traced in the dust, moments before I arrived.
local:2.line: 'These are *local* words — borrow them off this peak and they go silent.'

tend:2.en: I asked Xiaoxing why certain ancient scrolls were wrapped in damp cloth while others lay bare. She told me that living words — those still carrying spiritual breath — *tend* to dry out and crack if left unsealed, the same way a herb loses its scent without soil. A dead word, she said softly, needs no such care.
tend:2.cnHint: 小星解释说，有灵气的字诀____会因风干而失效，就像草药离土便失去药性，所以需要湿布封存。
tend:2.hook: One bare scroll, she had not yet touched, was already crumbling at the edges.
tend:2.line: 'Living words *tend* to fade faster than the ones that were never truly woken.'

term:2.en: The first page of the archive ledger listed every word a new disciple must learn before the season ended — each one labeled with a small circle, each circle empty until mastered. At the top, in Master Qingwu's own hand, was the *term* for this opening period: the Hollow Month, when a disciple's vessel is most ready to receive. Mine had already half passed.
term:2.cnHint: 档案总册首页列出了新弟子在这段入门____内须掌握的全部字诀，师尊将此阶段亲笔命名为'空月'。
term:2.hook: Three circles on my page had filled themselves in without my knowledge.
term:2.line: 'The *term* is short — if the Hollow Month closes before you are ready, it does not return.'

reduce:2.en: Deep in the Archive Grotto, I found a crumbling scroll sealed with jade dust. The text described how a cultivator could *reduce* the weight of a spiritual herb by half, drawing out its purest essence before refining. I copied the formula with trembling hands. Something ancient watched from the shadows.
reduce:2.cnHint: 我在藏经石窟中发现了一卷残卷，记载着如何____草药的重量以提炼其精华。
reduce:2.hook: The jade seal cracked the moment I finished copying.
reduce:2.line: 'You must *reduce* the herb to its core before the moon sets,' said Master Qingwu.

process:2.en: Shen Wujiu spread three worn scrolls across the stone floor of the lower archive. 'The *process* of awakening a word-herb takes seven steps,' he said quietly. 'Miss even one, and the formula turns to ash.' I watched his steady hands move from scroll to scroll, mapping a path I had never seen before.
process:2.cnHint: 师兄向我展示觉醒字草的____，共有七个步骤，缺一不可。
process:2.hook: The seventh step had been torn cleanly away.
process:2.line: 'The *process* is longer than it looks — do not rush the third step,' said Shen Wujiu.

able:2.en: The relic chest had been locked for three generations. Master Qingwu placed one finger on its brass face, and a soft hum rose through the stone room. 'Only someone carrying the Cloud Sea resonance will be *able* to open it,' she said. She stepped back and looked at me. The hum grew louder.
able:2.cnHint: 师尊说，只有与云海宗有共鸣之人才____开启那口古箱。
able:2.hook: Every candle in the archive went out at once.
able:2.line: 'You may be *able* to read what no one here has read in years,' said Master Qingwu.

drive:2.en: A folded letter lay inside the hollow base of a stone pillar — someone had left it decades ago. The words inside were simple: a single *drive* to find the missing half of the Formless Sutra had led its author deep into the Outer Peaks, and they had never returned. I folded the letter back with care.
drive:2.cnHint: 一封藏在石柱底部的信揭示，某人曾受一种强烈的____支配，只身前往外峰寻找残卷。
drive:2.hook: The handwriting matched the name carved above the archive door.
drive:2.line: 'What *drive* could push a disciple to leave without a word?' whispered Xiaoxing.

face:2.en: The oldest scroll in the grotto bore no title. Its outer layer had worn smooth as silk, but the inner *face* of the parchment still held faint silver characters that shifted when I breathed on them. Xiaoxing pressed close beside me, her voice hushed. The characters rearranged themselves into a warning.
face:2.cnHint: 那卷最古老的残卷，其羊皮纸的内____上仍隐约可见会移动的银色文字。
face:2.hook: The warning named a disciple who stood in this very room.
face:2.line: 'Look at the inner *face* of the page — do you see the silver words?' said Xiaoxing.

possible:2.en: Master Qingwu held the broken tablet to the pale window light. 'Is it *possible* that a second copy was made before the original was split?' she asked, not speaking to either of us. The dust motes in the beam of light hung perfectly still, as though the archive itself was waiting for her answer.
possible:2.cnHint: 师尊凝视着残片，低声询问在原本被分开之前，是否____存在第二份拓本。
possible:2.hook: A faint echo answered her from somewhere below the floor.
possible:2.line: 'It is *possible* that the missing half never left this mountain,' said Master Qingwu.

similar:2.en: Two fragments rested side by side on the reading table. Their script looked *similar* at first glance, yet Shen Wujiu pointed out that every third character was subtly different — a different hand, a different era. 'One was copied from the other,' he said softly, 'but which one came first?' The afternoon clouds thickened outside.
similar:2.cnHint: 两块残片上的字迹看起来____，但师兄发现每隔三个字便存在细微差异。
similar:2.hook: The older fragment began to glow along its broken edge.
similar:2.line: 'The brushwork is *similar*, but these two scrolls were not written by the same hand,' said Shen Wujiu.

involve:2.en: Xiaoxing unrolled a narrow scroll she had found behind a loose brick. The cipher it contained was unlike any I had studied. 'Every advanced formula must *involve* at least one word from the Forbidden Tier,' she read aloud, her voice dropping at the end. We looked at each other. Neither of us knew what the Forbidden Tier was.
involve:2.cnHint: 小星发现的残卷写道，每一种高阶丹方都必然____至少一个禁级字草。
involve:2.hook: A single black feather drifted down from the ceiling above us.
involve:2.line: 'Does this path truly *involve* the Forbidden Tier?' Xiaoxing asked, her voice barely a breath.

risk:2.en: The sealed scroll had not been touched in a hundred years. Shen Wujiu warned me that to open it without a guiding word was to *risk* losing one's voice forever. I steadied my breath, pressed my palm to the cold jade cover, and whispered the only herb-word I knew. The seal cracked — and then held, trembling.
risk:2.cnHint: 打开封印卷轴需要付出代价，师兄警告我这样做会____永远失去声音。
risk:2.hook: A thin line of black smoke curled up from the crack and did not fade.
risk:2.line: 'You *risk* your voice every time you open a seal without permission.'

success:2.en: Xiaoxing had tried the mirror-lock puzzle four times and failed each time. I traced the word for 'light' along the stone frame with one slow finger, and the mirror swung open. She stared at me, then smiled. Master Qingwu recorded the moment in his ledger without looking up — but his brush moved quickly, a sign of *success*.
success:2.cnHint: 我解开了镜锁难题，师尊在账簿上快速记录了这次____。
success:2.hook: Inside the mirror chamber, a second ledger lay open to a page with my name already written.
success:2.line: 'True *success* leaves a mark the mountain remembers.'

group:2.en: Master Qingwu gathered every new disciple at the Edge Pavilion at dawn. Our *group* was small — seven in all — and we stood in a line above the sea of clouds, each holding a paper card printed with a single word. The word on mine was blank. No one else's was blank. The wind moved through us like a question.
group:2.cnHint: 清晨，我们这个小____在悬崖亭聚集，只有我的词卡是空白的。
group:2.hook: Master Qingwu looked at my blank card the longest, then folded his hands and said nothing.
group:2.line: 'A *group* that shares one word can move a mountain — remember that.'

course:2.en: The first lesson was not reading — it was walking. The stone path spiraled up the inner peak for half a day, and Master Qingwu called this the *course* of roots: every herb-word had to be carried in the body before it could be spoken. By the time I reached the top, a single character glowed faintly on my wrist.
course:2.cnHint: 第一堂课是沿石径攀登，师尊称之为根系____，走完后我的手腕上出现了发光的字符。
course:2.hook: The character on my wrist was not in any scroll I had ever seen.
course:2.line: 'The *course* of a true word always runs through the body first.'

relationship:2.en: Xiaoxing showed me two herb-words carved side by side on a stone tablet near the archive gate. 'See how their roots touch?' she said. The *relationship* between the two words made a third meaning that neither word held alone — something close to 'shelter.' I copied both into my notebook. Outside, a cloud the shape of a roof drifted past.
relationship:2.cnHint: 小星指出两个草药字的字根相触，它们之间的____产生了第三种含义。
relationship:2.hook: The cloud stopped moving and held its roof-shape for far too long.
relationship:2.line: 'The *relationship* between two words can hold more power than either one alone.'

form:2.en: The enrollment record asked for name, mountain of origin, and spirit-root type. But the last line of the *form* was a blank beside the words 'your first spoken word in the Sect.' I did not know what to write. Shen Wujiu leaned over and whispered that most disciples leave it empty. Most, he said. Not all.
form:2.cnHint: 入门登记____的最后一栏要填写"在门派开口说的第一个字"，师兄说大多数弟子都空着。
form:2.hook: When I finally set down the brush, the ink on that last line shimmered gold for one breath and then turned black.
form:2.line: 'Fill every part of the *form* — the blank lines remember what you leave in them.'

interest:2.en: The archive elder watched me pull the same scroll from the shelf three mornings in a row. On the fourth morning he set a different scroll beside it without a word — older, water-stained, and locked with a bone clasp. 'Your *interest* in the thunder-herb family has been noted,' he said, and walked away before I could ask how he knew.
interest:2.cnHint: 档案长注意到我对雷草一族的____，悄悄为我放了一卷更古老、加锁的卷轴。
interest:2.hook: The bone clasp was already warm, as though someone had held it recently.
interest:2.line: '*Interest* shown three mornings in a row is a kind of vow around here.'

simply:2.en: Shen Wujiu watched me struggle with the water-word for an hour, layering breath over breath and getting only mist. He crossed the room, touched the paper once, and the word bloomed into a small still pool that reflected the ceiling perfectly. 'You are trying too hard,' he said. 'Some words *simply* open when you stop pushing.'
simply:2.cnHint: 师兄轻触纸张，水字立刻绽放，他告诉我有些字____会在你停止用力时自然打开。
simply:2.hook: The tiny pool in the paper did not dry — it was still there the next morning, cold and perfectly clear.
simply:2.line: 'Some doors *simply* open — all you have to do is stop blocking them.'

put:2.en: The old scroll room smelled of pine and rain. I found a narrow shelf carved into the stone wall and *put* the fragile herb-formula there, where morning light could dry its ink without burning the leaf. Xiaoxing watched in silence, then gave a small nod of approval. The shelf had been empty for a long time.
put:2.cnHint: 我把珍贵的草药卷轴____在石墙的窄架上，让晨光烘干墨迹。
put:2.hook: Behind the shelf, a hollow space held one more scroll — sealed in red wax.
put:2.line: '*Put* it on the high shelf, where only careful hands can reach.'

difference:2.en: Shen Wujiu laid two herb-scrolls side by side on the study table. To my untrained eye they looked the same, but he traced the strokes slowly. 'Feel the *difference* in the final curve,' he said. One curve opened like a wing; the other closed like a fist. One word healed. The other did not.
difference:2.cnHint: 师兄让我感受两份卷轴末笔之间的____，两者看似相同，效果却截然不同。
difference:2.hook: A cold draft moved through the sealed room, though no window was open.
difference:2.line: 'The *difference* in one stroke decides whether the word heals or harms.'

lack:2.en: Master Qingwu set three herb-vials on the stone bench and studied me in silence. 'Your energy is steady,' she said at last, 'but you show a *lack* of stillness in the final breath.' She did not say it harshly. She said it the way a gardener names thin soil — simply, so the plant can be moved. I bowed and said nothing.
lack:2.cnHint: 青雾师尊指出我修炼中____沉静之心，语气平和却令人警醒。
lack:2.hook: That night the candle in my room burned without any wind — yet it bent west.
lack:2.line: 'A *lack* of stillness in one breath can undo a whole season of work.'

case:2.en: Xiaoxing carried a small wooden *case* to the archive door and set it down with both hands. Inside, wrapped in dry leaves, lay a half-burned scroll that no one had opened in forty years. The archivist tilted her lamp close, then stepped back without a word. Some discoveries, it seemed, required permission from above.
case:2.cnHint: 小星带来一只木____，里面藏着一卷四十年无人开启的半焦残卷。
case:2.hook: The lock on the archive door turned by itself before anyone touched it.
case:2.line: 'This *case* has not been opened since the year the east peak went dark.'

sure:2.en: I read the recovery formula three times before writing it down. Shen Wujiu looked over my shoulder. 'Are you *sure* the third herb goes before the second?' he asked quietly. I checked again. My hand had reversed them without my noticing — a small error that would have turned a healing word into a numbing one. I thanked him. He just shrugged.
sure:2.cnHint: 师兄提醒我核查药方顺序，我才发现自己无意中将第三味草药与第二味____写反了。
sure:2.hook: On the page beneath mine, the same reversal appeared — in someone else's old ink.
sure:2.line: 'Are you *sure* that order is right — check the third herb one more time.'

enough:2.en: The candle burned low as I copied the flight-formula for the fourth time. Xiaoxing glanced at my work and said, 'That is *enough* for tonight — your strokes grow thin when you are tired.' I wanted to argue, but I looked at the last line and saw she was right. Thin strokes made weak words. Weak words made no wind.
enough:2.cnHint: 小星告诉我今晚的练习已经____，因为疲惫时笔画会变细，弱笔写不出有力的字。
enough:2.hook: As I set down the brush, every candle in the hall dimmed at once.
enough:2.line: '*Enough* for tonight — a tired hand writes words the wind will not obey.'

attention:2.en: Master Qingwu stood before the shelf of sealed jars and spoke without turning. 'Pay *attention* to the jar on the far left,' she said. I looked. The seal was the same pale wax as the others, yet the herb inside had turned faintly silver overnight. No one had touched it. No one had opened it. The room had been locked since dawn.
attention:2.cnHint: 青雾师尊要我把____集中在最左边的那只封口药罐上，那里发生了无人能解释的变化。
attention:2.hook: The silver herb began to glow the moment my eyes fully settled on it.
attention:2.line: 'Give your full *attention* to the far jar — and do not look away.'

certain:2.en: Shen Wujiu spread the old sect map on the floor and pointed to a blank ring near the mountain's root. 'I am *certain* this passage was sealed after the last storm season,' he said. The blank ring held no label, no route, no warning sign — only a faint outline, as if someone had drawn it and then tried to erase the memory of doing so.
certain:2.cnHint: 无咎师兄____地指出地图上那段无名通道曾在某次风暴后被封闭，却没有留下任何标记。
certain:2.hook: When he lifted his hand from the map, his fingertip had turned cold.
certain:2.line: 'I am *certain* this passage was closed — but not why, and not by whom.'

enable:2.en: Deep in the sect library, I found a scroll sealed with silver thread. Shen Wujiu said the words inside could *enable* a disciple to read the wind itself — to feel where each cloud current led before stepping onto it. I broke the seal. The characters glowed faint blue, then went dark.
enable:2.cnHint: 在藏经阁深处，我发现一卷银线封印的残卷，据说其中的字句能____弟子读懂风语。
enable:2.hook: The last word on the scroll had been carefully cut away.
enable:2.line: 'These words *enable* you to hear what the mountain refuses to say.'

simple:2.en: Xiaoxing handed me a single-page chart she had found tucked behind a cracked wall stone. The diagram looked *simple* — one circle, three lines, four small words. Yet Master Qingwu had searched for this formula for twenty years. I set it on the reading table, and the candle flame turned green.
simple:2.cnHint: 小星在石缝里找到一张看似____的单页图表，却是师尊寻觅二十年的秘方。
simple:2.hook: The green flame cast no shadow on the wall behind it.
simple:2.line: 'Do not mistake *simple* for weak — one word can split a cloud.'

several:2.en: In the lower archive, I found *several* torn pages stuffed inside an old ink jar. Each page held half a word — spiritual characters split down the middle, as if someone had divided them on purpose. Shen Wujiu went quiet when he saw them and slowly closed the jar.
several:2.cnHint: 在藏经阁下层，我在旧墨罐里发现了____张残页，每张都写着被刻意劈开的灵字。
several:2.hook: The ink inside the jar was still wet.
several:2.line: 'I have seen *several* of these jars — none of them were left by accident.'

struggle:2.en: The ancient text described a disciple whose *struggle* to master one single word lasted nine winters. She could not shape the sound right; her breath kept breaking the character apart. At last she carved it into her own walking staff. That staff, the text said, still stood at the peak — unburned.
struggle:2.cnHint: 古籍中记载了一位弟子为掌握一个字而历经九年____的故事，她的手杖至今仍立于山顶。
struggle:2.hook: The page that named her had been soaked until the name washed away.
struggle:2.line: 'Every *struggle* with a word leaves a mark the word remembers.'

decision:2.en: The scroll offered two paths forward, written in red and black ink side by side. One word led to healing; the other led to flight. A note at the bottom, in Master Qingwu's own hand, read: every *decision* made here echoes in the clouds below. I stared at both words until my lamp burned out.
decision:2.cnHint: 残卷上并排写着两条路，而师尊亲笔注明：在此做出的每一个____都会在云海中回响。
decision:2.hook: When the lamp died, only the red word remained faintly visible.
decision:2.line: 'A *decision* made in haste feeds the wrong word inside you.'

kid:2.en: A small note fell from between the pages — written in uneven, unsteady strokes, clearly by a child. Xiaoxing read it aloud: a young *kid* had once sneaked into the library at night to copy a single healing word, hoping to save a sick bird. The bird's name was written at the bottom of the note.
kid:2.cnHint: 一张从书页间落出的纸条，出自一个小____之手，他深夜潜入藏经阁只为抄下一个治愈之字。
kid:2.hook: The bird's name was the same as a missing senior disciple.
kid:2.line: 'Even a *kid* who copies one word in the dark plants a seed in the mountain.'

ability:2.en: The scroll I unrolled had only one line, written in deep violet ink: true *ability* with words is not speed, not force — it is knowing which word to leave unspoken. Below it, someone had pressed a dried cloud-petal as a mark. I touched it, and it crumbled to pale ash in my palm.
ability:2.cnHint: 我展开的残卷只有一行字：真正的____不在于速度或力量，而在于知道哪个字该保持沉默。
ability:2.hook: The ash spelled out a character I had never been taught.
ability:2.line: '*Ability* without stillness is just noise wearing the shape of a word.'

task:2.en: Pinned to the innermost shelf was a list in faded ink. Each line described a *task* assigned to a disciple: find the echo word, seal the hollow syllable, return the borrowed tone. Most lines had been crossed out. The last one had no name beside it — and it was not crossed out.
task:2.cnHint: 藏经阁最内层的书架上钉着一张褪色的清单，每行都是分配给弟子的一项____，最后一项没有署名，也没有被划掉。
task:2.hook: The last task was written in ink that still smelled of rain.
task:2.line: 'A *task* left unsigned is a task the mountain is still waiting for someone to claim.'

popular:2.en: In the archive hall, I found a shelf of scrolls worn smooth by many hands. Shen Wujiu said the most *popular* formula among disciples was the Wind-Step verse — copied so often the ink had faded to grey. I reached for it, and the scroll trembled, as if it remembered every reader before me.
popular:2.cnHint: 在藏经阁，我发现了一卷在弟子中最____的咒文，它因被反复抄录而墨迹已淡。
popular:2.hook: Then the scroll fell open to a page no one had copied.
popular:2.line: 'The *popular* ones are worn out — read the ones no one else dared touch.'

current:2.en: Master Qingwu led me to a narrow bridge above the sea of clouds. Below, a slow *current* of white mist moved like a river with no shore. She placed a single leaf on the air and it followed that invisible path exactly. 'The clouds have their own grammar,' she said. Far off, the leaf vanished without falling.
current:2.cnHint: 清雾师尊带我观看云海中那道____，将叶片置于其上，叶随无形之道漂去。
current:2.hook: The mist shifted, and the bridge was no longer where it had been.
current:2.line: 'Follow the *current* — it knows the mountain's true shape.'

difficult:2.en: The scroll assigned to me was written in an old hand, full of turns and crossings. Xiaoxing leaned over my shoulder and smiled. 'That one is *difficult* — even Shen Wujiu spent three days on the first line.' I read the first word aloud, and the candle flame bent toward me, listening.
difficult:2.cnHint: 小星告诉我，我分到的那卷功法____，连师兄也花了三天才读懂第一行。
difficult:2.hook: Outside, wind pressed against the archive door as if something wanted in.
difficult:2.line: 'It is *difficult*, yes — but only the first word costs you everything.'

amount:2.en: Shen Wujiu poured a small measure of luminous powder onto the scale. 'The *amount* matters as much as the word itself,' he said. 'Too little and the formula sleeps. Too much and it burns the one who speaks it.' I watched the needle settle, and my own pulse settled with it — then jumped.
amount:2.cnHint: 师兄在秤上称量灵粉，告诉我配制咒文时，灵粉的____与字句本身同等重要。
amount:2.hook: One grain rolled off the scale and dissolved in the air before it landed.
amount:2.line: 'The right *amount* is the line between healing and harm.'

point:2.en: Master Qingwu pressed one finger to the centre of the old map. 'This is the *point* all cloud-paths cross,' she said. 'Miss it and you circle the mountain for years.' The spot was unmarked — just a small worn circle left by generations of fingers before hers. I pressed my own finger there, and felt the mountain breathe.
point:2.cnHint: 清雾师尊指出地图上所有云路交汇的____，那里没有标注，只有无数前人留下的磨痕。
point:2.hook: When I lifted my hand, the circle had grown slightly larger.
point:2.line: 'Every path has one *point* where the choice becomes real.'

role:2.en: Xiaoxing handed me a folded note she had found inside a cracked wall-brick. It listed three names — none of them mine — and beside each, a single word for their *role* in a ritual no one had performed in a hundred years. My name was not there. But the space below the third name was blank and waiting.
role:2.cnHint: 小星从砖缝中找到一张旧纸条，上面列着三人在某场仪式中各自的____，最后一行是空白。
role:2.hook: The ink on the blank line was still faintly wet.
role:2.line: 'Everyone in that ritual had a *role* — someone chose to leave one empty.'

survey:2.en: Master Qingwu led me to the Edge Pavilion, where the mountain dropped away into white mist. She asked me to *survey* the shelf of scroll cases below and note which seals had gone dark. I counted seven cold seals among hundreds of glowing ones. Seven words, lost.
survey:2.cnHint: 师尊命我在悬崖阁____那排卷轴架，记下封印已灭的卷轴。
survey:2.hook: The seventh dark seal pulsed once, then split clean down the middle.
survey:2.line: '*Survey* every shelf before you touch a single scroll,' said Master Qingwu.

care:2.en: Xiaoxing passed me a torn scroll with both hands, the way one carries a wounded bird. 'Copy it before the ink fades,' she said. I worked through the night, and the *care* I gave each stroke seemed to slow the fading. By dawn, the text still breathed.
care:2.cnHint: 小星叮嘱我抄录残卷时要多加____，因为墨迹正在消退。
care:2.hook: When I lifted my brush for the last stroke, the candle flame bent toward the words.
care:2.line: 'Copy it with *care*, or the meaning will be the first thing lost,' Xiaoxing said.

state:2.en: Shen Wujiu pressed his palm to the sealed archive door and closed his eyes. 'The door reads your *state* of mind,' he told me. 'Bring greed in and it stays shut.' I stilled my breathing, thought of nothing but the words inside, and the door opened like a slow exhale.
state:2.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，档案室的门会感应进入者的心理____，贪念会让它紧闭不开。
state:2.hook: Behind the door, one lantern was already lit — and no one had been inside for a year.
state:2.line: 'Calm your *state* of mind first; the archive decides the rest,' Shen Wujiu said.

impact:2.en: The ancient formula hit the stone floor of the copy room when I knocked it from its stand. The *impact* shook loose three dried petals pressed between the pages — petals I did not recognise, black at the edges and faintly warm. Xiaoxing went very still when she saw them.
impact:2.cnHint: 我不小心碰落了古老卷轴，____使夹在其中的三片干花瓣散落出来。
impact:2.hook: Xiaoxing whispered one word, and the petals rose an inch above the floor.
impact:2.line: 'That *impact* may have woken something that was meant to sleep,' Xiaoxing said.

reason:2.en: Master Qingwu set a blank scroll before me and said nothing. I waited for instruction, but none came. After a long silence I understood — the *reason* she gave me no task was the task itself. I wrote the first word I truly needed, and the scroll began to glow on its own.
reason:2.cnHint: 师尊没有交代任务，而____正是她沉默本身——我需要自己找到该写的字。
reason:2.hook: The glow spread to every blank scroll on the shelf, one by one.
reason:2.line: 'The *reason* I say nothing is that the answer must come from you,' said Master Qingwu.

close:2.en: The restricted shelf stood at the far end of the archive, but the air near it felt *close* and heavy, as if the words stored there pressed outward against the dark. Shen Wujiu stopped three steps away and would not move nearer. I asked why. He only shook his head.
close:2.cnHint: 禁架附近的空气令人感到压抑____，师兄在距它三步处停下，不肯再靠近。
close:2.hook: From somewhere inside the restricted shelf, a page turned by itself.
close:2.line: 'Stay *close* to me and do not reach for anything on that shelf,' Shen Wujiu said.

individual:2.en: Each scroll in the Hall of Origins bore a single word, and Master Qingwu said every *individual* word there had once belonged to a real disciple — their last spoken breath preserved in ink. I touched none of them. The hall was too quiet for a place full of voices.
individual:2.cnHint: 起源殿的每一个____字卷都封存着一位弟子最后的声息，我不敢触碰任何一卷。
individual:2.hook: One scroll near the entrance trembled when I spoke my own name aloud.
individual:2.line: 'Each *individual* scroll here is a life — read them as such,' Master Qingwu said.

area:2.en: Xiaoxing drew a careful circle on the archive floor with white chalk and told me to sit inside it. 'This *area* is sealed,' she explained, handing me the damaged text. 'Whatever the scroll releases stays within the line.' I opened the cover, and something cold and bright rose from the page.
area:2.cnHint: 小星在地板上画了一个封印____，要我坐在其中再打开那卷受损的古籍。
area:2.hook: The chalk line held — but it also began, very slowly, to crack.
area:2.line: 'Do not leave this *area* until every last word on that page has settled,' Xiaoxing said.

term:0.en: Inside the Sutra Vault, dusty shelves curved upward like ribs of a sleeping giant. I opened a half-burnt scroll and found a single *term* written in silver ink — one word that named a forbidden formula. Master Qingwu had warned us: some words carry weight that crushes the unprepared.
term:0.cnHint: 我在藏经阁的残卷中发现了一个危险的____，银墨字迹令人心悸。
term:0.hook: The silver ink began to glow the moment I read it aloud.
term:0.line: 'That *term* has not been spoken here in three hundred years,' said Master Qingwu.

similar:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread two scrolls side by side on the stone reading table. The characters looked *similar* at first — nearly twins — yet one promised flight and the other promised ruin. Xiaoxing leaned close, her breath held, tracing the single brushstroke that divided healing from harm.
similar:0.cnHint: 师兄将两卷残卷并排，发现它们的字形____，却含义截然不同。
similar:0.hook: Somewhere above, a shelf collapsed under no visible weight.
similar:0.line: 'They are *similar*, yes — but only one of them is safe,' said Shen Wujiu.
